summary: The described cost is gone (shipped in 60633eff3 / #710; the Hub pin 7bc39eec3 includes it). On a black-holed network the web boot gate now releases after about 8 s, down from 30-60 s. In cookie mode the session restore runs with an 8 s request deadline (HOSTED_ACCESS_CHECK_DEADLINE_MS), and the gate awaits bootstrapAccess(), which settles on the account answer before the directory read. A timeout publishes 'unavailable' with the access retry armed (1 s base backoff), and HostedHubRoot renders 'Retry Hub'. An authenticated account with a loading directory renders the app shell or the node-restoring surface, not the boot surface. The chunks the gate loads (HostedHubRoot, hostedRootAppShell) are in the PWA precache, so they cannot re-stall the gate. Mobile has its own 8 s launch-decision bound plus the bearer decision deadline. Tests cover the bound, the settle-before-directory behaviour and the bearer decision deadline. One adjacent path is still uncovered: the signed-out branch (see fixDefects). It is low value and does not affect the headline scenario.

evidence.note: REQUEST_DEADLINE_MS stays 30 s. HostedHubReadOptions.deadlineMs lets a read give up sooner.

#request arms its timer with Math.min(REQUEST_DEADLINE_MS, options.deadlineMs ?? REQUEST_DEADLINE_MS) and covers body consumption. restoreSession (api.ts:996-1004) and listNodes (api.ts:2476-2481) forward deadlineMs.
#accessCheckOptions returns { deadlineMs: 8000 } in cookie mode until a check has timed out. Used by #restoreAccess (state.ts:750) and #resumeBrowser (state.ts:2054).
bootstrap() publishes #bootstrapAccessPromise, and bootstrapAccess() returns it. #restoreAccess calls accessSettled at state.ts:772, before awaiting #refreshDirectoryWith at state.ts:773.
In bearer mode, #armAccessDecisionDeadline publishes 'unavailable' at 8 s and releases the gate without abandoning a request that may rotate the token.
The directory prefetch rides beside the restore at the full deadline and is abandoned on failure, so no gate waits on it.
The gate awaits bootstrapWithHostedReadCache(() => hostedHubController.bootstrapAccess()). Called from apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:199.
HostedHubRoot and hostedRootAppShell, which the gate also awaits, are precached by the service worker, so on a black-holed link they come from cache.

With the account unavailable, the auth surface renders 'Retry Hub'. With the account authenticated and the directory not ready, the RootAppShell (hosted-cached) or HostedNodeRestoringSurface renders, not the boot surface.
The mobile launch gate is bounded by HOSTED_LAUNCH_DECISION_DEADLINE_MS = 8_000 (launchDecision.ts:20), even though ensureMobileHostedSession awaits the full bootstrap().

Tests cover: the gate settling before the directory read, settling on unavailable without a directory read, the 8 s bound followed by the full deadline after a timeout, and the bearer decision deadline including late success or late 401.
Uncovered path: after a 401, the gate (bootstrap's finally) still waits for getBootstrapAvailability, which has the default 30 s deadline (api.ts:904-913).

fixDefects: Minor uncovered path (the auditor said none). In #restoreAccess's session-failure branch (packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:776-790), a 401 restore chains getBootstrapAvailability(operation.signal), which has the default 30 s REQUEST_DEADLINE_MS (api.ts:904-913). accessSettled is not called on this branch, so bootstrapAccess() and the web boot gate only release after that probe. A signed-out or expired-session visitor without a remembered read cache can therefore sit on AppBootLoadingSurface for up to ~30 s if /api/auth/session answers 401 but /api/auth/bootstrap-status then stalls. This is the same partial-stall pattern the finding counted for /api/nodes. It does not arise on a fully black-holed link, the headline case, because the 401 never arrives there. Cosmetic: the bootstrapAccess JSDoc (state.ts:639-648, introduced alongside 8c42d3334) is orphaned above accessCheckPending()'s own JSDoc, so bootstrapAccess() at state.ts:659 has no doc.
implementationSketch: 1) api.ts: change getBootstrapAvailability(signal?) to getBootstrapAvailability(signal?, options?: HostedHubReadOptions) and forward deadlineMs to #request, as restoreSession does at api.ts:1000-1004. 2) state.ts #restoreAccess session-failure branch (~state.ts:783-789): pass { deadlineMs: HOSTED_ACCESS_CHECK_DEADLINE_MS } to getBootstrapAvailability. It is a public, idempotent probe that already falls back to false on any failure, so a short bound changes nothing but the wait. In bearer mode the DPoP mint signing runs before the timer and is unaffected. 3) Move the orphaned JSDoc block at state.ts:639-648 to directly above bootstrapAccess() at state.ts:659. Tests: in state.test.ts (cookie mode), restoreSession rejects HostedHubApiError('session_invalid', 401); assert getBootstrapAvailability received { deadlineMs: HOSTED_ACCESS_CHECK_DEADLINE_MS }; then with fake timers and a getBootstrapAvailability that rejects with a timeout, assert bootstrapAccess() settles with accountStatus 'signed-out' and bootstrapAvailable false. In api.test.ts, extend the existing deadline test (~api.test.ts:992) to cover getBootstrapAvailability. Validate with focused vitest runs of packages/client-runtime authorization tests only.
decisionReason: Only a request deadline on a public availability probe and a doc move. Session, credential and E2EE semantics and hosted lifecycle ownership are unchanged, and the timeout fallback (bootstrapAvailable=false) is existing behaviour.
correction: The auditor's DONE is correct for the described scenario. They missed that the signed-out branch of the same gate (401, then getBootstrapAvailability at the default 30 s deadline) is still awaited before the gate releases. Their api.ts timer line (3047) is the Math.min argument inside the setTimeout call at 3042-3048.
